metadata.title: Google to Spend $15 Billion in Malaysia Data Center Expansion

content.text:
(Bloomberg) -- Alphabet Inc.'s Google said it plans to spend $15 billion to expand data center and cloud operations in Malaysia as the artificial intelligence boom fuels demand for digital infrastructure.

The company will build new computing hubs and invest in local water security, power generation and training of Malaysia's residents, according to a statement on Wednesday. The investments are set to occur during 2027 and 2028, it said.
Google joins other global tech firms in expanding in the country, attractive for its relatively low cost and reliable infrastructure, and close proximity to business centers such as Singapore. Malaysia has emerged as Southeast Asia's main data center hub, attracting companies from Oracle Corp. and Amazon.com Inc. to Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. and ByteDance Ltd. — all needing more storage and processing capacity as data-hungry AI services gain users.
The construction phase of the new campuses over the next two years is set to add $1.1 billion to Malaysia's economy and support more than 37,000 local jobs per year, Google said. Once operational, the data centers are expected to sustain more than 9,000 local jobs a year, including technicians, mechanical and electrical engineers, logistics and security managers.
The outlay "reflects our confidence in the strength of Malaysia's leadership, its skilled workforce, and enthusiasm for digital transformation," Ruth Porat, Alphabet's chief investment officer, said at an event in Kuala Lumpur attended by Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar said Google's investment respects Malaysia's resources and shows belief in its people. "Our nation possesses the stability, the talent, the ambition to be a premier digital powerhouse in Southeast Asia," he said.
Earlier this week, Google announced $160 million in funding for shared water infrastructure in Negeri Sembilan, a state just south of Kuala Lumpur, to support its planned data center operations while also serving local communities.
